page.layout: One column of running text, the whole page; no marginal notes. Below the text: the signature "K 3" and the catchword "dicis" at the right.

main_text.p: addita theriaca, feruetiq; cinere coctum & applicatum, falutare praesidium proditur. Etenim trib. horis uirus extrahere, ac pus maturare fertur. Carbunculos ad suppura-tionem perducit, finapi & ruta fyluestris, addito melle. Eruum item ex uino, lupini impositi ipsos rumpunt. Idem praestant nu ces peruetetes, panaces, fimum quoq; co-lumbinum, cum lini semine ex aceto mul-so. Ruta per se, uisco addito, ut haereat, plu-rimum prodest, teste Paulo Ægineta. Ad abscessus omnes & carbunculos pestilen-tes commendatur plurimum oleum scor-pionum, cui theriacę media pars fuerit ad-dita, una cum sambuci floribus, & hyperici coma. Clarisimo praesidio dat [?] potio, quae haber ramenti cornu cerui drachmam, spe cierū diamargariti frigidi Scrup. i. succi li-monij [?], aut citrei, aut aracij, aut mali punici acidi lemunciam, (uel horum omnium pe-nuria) syrupi limonum, aut ex acetositate citrei, uel acetati simplicis, uel deniq; e suc co oxalidis sexcunciam, cui adde myrrhae drachmam, & feminis cardui benedicti tan tundem. Ad ignem protinus bibitur, cum inguina morbo tentari sentiuntur. Prompti[?]simū esse remedium a doctissimis me-

page.notes: Page number read as "149"; the last digit is slightly unclear in the scan. Running head "CAVSAS, PROGYMNASMATA." with the page number after it. "dat" and "Scrup. i." are read from a worn print. "limonij" and "Prompti[?]ssimū" are doubtful. The first line is a continuation from the previous page. Ends mid-word at "me-"; the catchword "dicis" starts the next page.
